## What changed

**A half-configured package looked fully installed, and the tool walked
straight into it.** On a real 19-step climb, step 7 failed here:

```
apt-get install … gitlab-ee=15.11.13-ee.0 → 100:
E: Sub-process /usr/bin/dpkg returned an error code (1)
```

dpkg had unpacked the new code but never finished configuring it, so
`gitlab-ctl reconfigure` — and with it the database migrations — never ran. The
schema stayed on 14.x while the code on disk was 15.11. `resume` did not notice,
and its first act is a backup:

```
PG::UndefinedTable: ERROR:  relation "design_management_repositories" does not exist
  …/lib/gitlab/gl_repository.rb:37 → backup/gitaly_backup.rb:70
```

So the one moment a backup mattered most was the moment there wasn't one.

The cause was one field. Detection asked dpkg only for `${Version}`, and dpkg
answers with a version for a half-configured package just as readily as for a
working one. It now asks for `${Status}` as well, and a new readiness check
blocks `run` and `resume` — before any backup, before any install, and not
waivable with `--force` — when the package is not actually configured:

```
✗  пакет GitLab   gitlab-ee 15.11.13-ee.0 распакован, но не настроен
                  (install ok unpacked)
   Что делать
     sudo dpkg --configure -a
```

Only the last two fields of `${Status}` decide. The first one is the *wanted*
state, and `apt-mark hold` — which this tool applies itself after the final
step — turns `install ok installed` into `hold ok installed`. Comparing the
whole string would have declared broken exactly the server that had just been
upgraded successfully.
